bibl.title: Early remodeling of the neocortex upon episodic memory encoding
bibl.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether the neocortex remodels early during memory encoding, rather than only weeks later during consolidation, and whether prefrontal activity is required for hippocampal engagement
span.quote: Here we report that long-term memory encoding can elicit early transcriptional, structural, and functional remodeling of the neocortex.

span.label: how does the prefrontal cortex contribute to long-term memory encoding, a role established correlationally but not mechanistically
span.quote: Nonetheless, the mechanisms by which the prefrontal cortex contributes to long-term memory encoding remain poorly understood.

span.label: shows encoding triggers transcriptional, structural and functional remodeling of medial prefrontal cortex within an hour, and that silencing those neurons during encoding blocks hippocampal activation and long-term memory
span.quote: Collectively, our results provide, to our knowledge, the first evidence that episodic memory encoding can induce early transcriptional, structural, and functional remodeling of the neocortex and identify the mPFC as a critical regulator of entorhinal–hippocampal circuit activation and the formation of long-term memory.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Here we report that long-term memory encoding can elicit early transcriptional, structural, and functional remodeling of the neocortex.

span.label: neocortical remodeling during episodic memory encoding
span.quote: Herein, we show that episodic memory encoding elicits early remodeling of neocortical circuits in mouse brain.

span.label: animal-experiment
span.quote: Parallel studies using genome-wide RNA sequencing, ultrastructural imaging, and whole-cell recording in wild-type mice suggest that contextual fear conditioning initiates a transcriptional program in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) that is accompanied by rapid expansion of the synaptic active zone and postsynaptic density, enhanced dendritic spine plasticity, and increased synaptic efficacy.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Excitatory mPFC neurons fire during encoding and drive activation of the entorhinal–hippocampal circuit, which in turn permits long-term memory to form
span.quote: Together, these data suggest that activity of excitatory mPFC neurons is required for entorhinal–hippocampal circuit activation during long-term associative memory encoding.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Encoding rapidly reprograms mPFC gene expression, and this transcriptional shift primes the local circuit for the structural and functional synaptic plasticity that follows
span.quote: These results suggest that the mPFC transcriptome is reprogrammed rapidly during associative memory encoding and that memory encoding primes the mPFC transcriptome for neuroplasticity.

span.label: an epoch is isolated rather than a region: excitatory prefrontal neurons are silenced only during the conditioning session, and memory is measured a day and a month afterwards
span.quote: To address the real-time contribution of the mPFC to long-term memory encoding, we performed temporally precise optogenetic inhibition of excitatory mPFC neurons during contextual fear conditioning. Using this approach, we found that real-time inhibition of the mPFC inhibited activation of the entorhinal–hippocampal circuit and impaired the formation of long-term associative memory.

span.label: the apparent contradiction with the standard model is resolved by indexing both claims to a stage rather than choosing between them
span.quote: As previous data indicate that late-stage memory consolidation requires hippocampus-driven reorganization of neocortical circuits ( 5 , 16 ), our data support a stage-dependent directionality model of memory-relevant information flow, in which neocortex-driven hippocampal activity is critical for memory encoding and formation, whereas hippocampus-driven neocortical reorganization mediates subsequent memory consolidation and storage.

span.label: five measurements at five levels of description are stacked on one claim - transcript, ultrastructure, spine morphology, synaptic current, and causal necessity
span.quote: Parallel studies using genome-wide RNA sequencing, ultrastructural imaging, and whole-cell recording in wild-type mice suggest that contextual fear conditioning initiates a transcriptional program in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) that is accompanied by rapid expansion of the synaptic active zone and postsynaptic density, enhanced dendritic spine plasticity, and increased synaptic efficacy.

span.label: the control condition is selected by measurement: context exposure produced more immediate-early gene expression than foot shock alone, so it becomes the conservative comparison throughout
span.quote: Additionally, as immediate early gene expression in the mPFC was significantly greater in context-exposed control animals relative to control animals exposed only to foot shock, context-exposed mice served as controls in subsequent experiments

span.label: unchanged total synapse density is what licenses the claim that existing circuitry was remodeled rather than new synapses added
span.quote: Finally, using parallel TEM ( Fig. S4 A and B ) and Golgi–Cox impregnation ( Fig. S4 C ), we found that despite the observed structural and functional plasticity induced in existing mPFC circuits following associative memory encoding, total synapse density in the mPFC remained unchanged.

span.label: the optogenetic manipulation is verified to have worked before its behavioural consequence is interpreted, by measuring the activity marker it was meant to suppress
span.quote: Next, we found that real-time optogenetic inhibition of the mPFC during contextual fear conditioning ( Fig. 4 D ) significantly reduced Zif268 expression in the mPFC of mice expressing eNpHR3.0-EYFP compared with mice expressing EYFP alone ( Fig. 4 E and F ), confirming that optogenetic inhibition prevented mPFC activation during long-term associative memory encoding.

span.label: the causal chain is traced outward one structure at a time - prefrontal, then entorhinal, then CA1 - rather than asserted from the endpoints
span.quote: Remarkably, we found that optogenetic inactivation of the mPFC during memory encoding significantly reduced the expression of Zif268 and synaptophysin in hippocampal area CA1 of mice expressing eNpHR3.0-EYFP compared with mice expressing EYFP alone ( Fig. 4 G and H ), suggesting that the mPFC is a critical regulator of hippocampal activation during long-term memory encoding.

span.label: behavioural specificity is checked against the two obvious confounds, locomotion and shock sensitivity, both of which are unaffected
span.quote: Importantly, neither basal locomotor activity ( Fig. 5 D ) nor sensitivity to foot shock ( Fig. 5 E ) differed significantly between the groups.

span.label: the transcriptional result is read as a direction rather than a list: plasticity-promoting genes up, plasticity-suppressing genes down
span.quote: Conversely, genes down-regulated in the mPFC during associative memory encoding are implicated in biological processes that have been shown to suppress synaptic plasticity and memory function, such as proliferation of microglia, activation of phagocytes, and apoptosis

span.label: sequencing results are confirmed on independent samples by a second assay before being built on
span.quote: Strikingly, we found that 342 genes (121 up-regulated, 221 down-regulated) were differentially expressed in the mPFC of mice that underwent fear conditioning compared with control animals

span.label: the encoding signature is compared with a disease signature and found to be its inverse, which converts a description into a prediction about pathology
span.quote: Finally, it is noteworthy that the pattern of gene expression we observed in the mPFC following memory encoding (i.e., up-regulation of synaptic plasticity-related genes, down-regulation of immune-related genes) is the inverse of the gene expression profile characteristic of AD ( 52 ) (i.e., up-regulation of immune-related genes, down-regulation of synaptic plasticity-related genes).

span.label: The study does not establish the relative contributions of other nodes of the distributed neocortical network to hippocampal-dependent memory formation.
span.note: what this limits: the specificity of the mPFC result: FUTURE STUDIES DELINEATING THE RELATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS OF VARIOUS NODES OF THE NEOCORTICAL NETWORK ... WILL LIKELY PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHT
span.quote: However, as memory encoding elicits the coordinated activity of widely distributed neural circuits ( 14 ), future studies delineating the relative contributions of various nodes of the neocortical network to hippocampal-dependent memory formation will likely provide critical insights into systems-level memory processing in the brain.

span.label: which neocortical inputs drive hippocampal activation at encoding was unknown, and this paper identifies one without excluding others
span.note: what this limits: the state of the question this paper answers: THE NEOCORTICAL INPUTS THAT DRIVE HIPPOCAMPAL ACTIVATION DURING MEMORY ENCODING ... REMAIN UNCLEAR
span.quote: However, the neocortical inputs that drive hippocampal activation during memory encoding, and thus regulate hippocampal-dependent memory formation, remain unclear.

span.label: encoding engages widely distributed circuits, so the relative contribution of each node remains to be apportioned
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - encoding ELICITS THE COORDINATED ACTIVITY OF WIDELY DISTRIBUTED NEURAL CIRCUITS, and the apportionment is not made here
span.quote: However, as memory encoding elicits the coordinated activity of widely distributed neural circuits ( 14 ), future studies delineating the relative contributions of various nodes of the neocortical network to hippocampal-dependent memory formation will likely provide critical insights into systems-level memory processing in the brain.

span.label: the mechanisms by which prefrontal pathology impairs memory in disease are still unclear, and the account offered is a possibility rather than a result
span.note: what this limits: the disease reading: THE mPFC IS AMONG THE FIRST BRAIN REGIONS TO DEVELOP AMYLOID-BETA PLAQUE DEPOSITION - an association offered, with the mechanism unestablished
span.quote: For instance, the mPFC is among the first brain regions to develop amyloid-β (Aβ) plaque deposition, an early pathological hallmark of AD

span.label: prior mechanistic work concentrated on consolidation and retrieval, so the encoding literature it is being compared against is thin
span.note: what this limits: the comparison with the prefrontal memory literature: MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION OF THE ROLE OF THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX IN MEMORY PROCESSING HAS LARGELY FOCUSED ON ITS ROLE IN MEMORY CONSOLIDATION AND RETRIEVAL, not encoding
span.quote: Interestingly however, mechanistic investigation of the role of the prefrontal cortex in memory processing has largely focused on its role in memory consolidation and retrieval.

span.label: genome-wide sequencing and gene-ontology network analysis, imported to turn a memory manipulation into a direction of transcriptional change rather than a candidate-gene test
span.quote: Gene ontology and gene network analyses of differentially expressed genes revealed that genes up-regulated in the mPFC during associative memory encoding form a highly interconnected network involved in biological processes that promote synaptic plasticity and memory formation, including synthesis of cAMP, neuritogenesis, long-term potentiation, and axon guidance

span.label: a light-driven chloride pump under a cell-type-specific promoter, which converts a regional correlation into an epoch-specific causal test
span.quote: Next, we used an in vivo optogenetic approach to permit real-time manipulation of excitatory mPFC neuronal activity in freely behaving mice.

span.label: context-exposed mice as the control group in the subsequent experiments, chosen over foot-shock-only animals because immediate early gene expression in mPFC was significantly greater in the context-exposed controls
span.note: eliminates: that the mPFC activation reflects the context or the foot shock on its own rather than the association between them - and the control is chosen to be the HARDER comparison of the two

span.label: memory encoding
span.quote: We found that associative memory encoding led to a rapid induction of ultrastructural synaptic plasticity in the mPFC, as contextual fear conditioning significantly expanded the size of the active zone and postsynaptic density ( Fig. 2 A and B and Fig. S2 A and B ) and increased the number of docked vesicles within individual mPFC synapses relative to controls

span.label: active zone
span.quote: We found that associative memory encoding led to a rapid induction of ultrastructural synaptic plasticity in the mPFC, as contextual fear conditioning significantly expanded the size of the active zone and postsynaptic density ( Fig. 2 A and B and Fig. S2 A and B ) and increased the number of docked vesicles within individual mPFC synapses relative to controls

span.label: neocortical remodeling - as a late consolidation process occurring weeks to months after encoding versus as an early process within the hour; the paper shows both exist and indexes them by stage
span.quote: As previous data indicate that late-stage memory consolidation requires hippocampus-driven reorganization of neocortical circuits ( 5 , 16 ), our data support a stage-dependent directionality model of memory-relevant information flow, in which neocortex-driven hippocampal activity is critical for memory encoding and formation, whereas hippocampus-driven neocortical reorganization mediates subsequent memory consolidation and storage.

span.label: the direction of hippocampal-neocortical influence - neocortex driving hippocampus at encoding, hippocampus driving neocortex at consolidation; the same pair of structures with the arrow reversed by stage
span.quote: According to the theoretical modeling work of Marr ( 43 ) and the standard model of systems-level memory consolidation ( 11 ), the hippocampus is believed to integrate input conveyed from distributed neocortical circuits with self-generated spatial information at the time of memory encoding to generate a unified, spatially contextualized memory trace.

span.label: dendritic spine - thin and plastic versus mushroom and stable; a morphological continuum read as two functional kinds
span.quote: Dendritic spines represent the postsynaptic component of excitatory synapses and exhibit morphological and functional continua, ranging from thin spines with a small head (i.e., thin spines) that are highly plastic and are hypothesized to underlie experience-dependent rewiring of neural circuits, to spines with a large, mushroom-like head (i.e., mushroom spines) that are more stable and are hypothesized to represent the physical substrates of long-term memories

span.label: synaptic change - as more synapses versus as remodeling of existing ones; unchanged total density decides it here
span.quote: Finally, using parallel TEM ( Fig. S4 A and B ) and Golgi–Cox impregnation ( Fig. S4 C ), we found that despite the observed structural and functional plasticity induced in existing mPFC circuits following associative memory encoding, total synapse density in the mPFC remained unchanged.

span.label: mEPSC frequency versus amplitude - presynaptic against postsynaptic locus, and only the first moved
span.quote: We found that mEPSC frequency, but not amplitude, was significantly increased at excitatory mPFC synapses 1 h following contextual fear conditioning relative to controls ( Fig. 3 C ), suggesting that associative memory encoding rapidly enhances the efficacy of excitatory presynaptic transmission in the mPFC.

span.label: recent versus remote long-term memory - 1 day against 30 days, tested separately because the standard model predicts prefrontal involvement only in the second
span.quote: In this regard, data in animal models suggest that glucose utilization ( 8 ), activity-dependent immediate early gene expression ( 9 , 10 ), and dendritic spine density ( 5 ) are increased in the prefrontal cortex following consolidation of remote, but not recent, long-term memory

span.quote: These findings suggest that encoding of long-term episodic memory is associated with early remodeling of neocortical circuits, identify the prefrontal cortex as a critical regulator of encoding-induced hippocampal activation and long-term memory formation, and have important implications for understanding memory processing in healthy and diseased brain states.

span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: neocortical remodeling during episodic memory encoding — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Prevailing theory suggests that episodic memory encoding is subserved by early remodeling of hippocampal circuits, whereas remodeling of the neocortex occurs weeks to months later to promote long-term memory storage and recall.

span.label: contradicts → the prevailing view that neocortical reorganization is limited to late stages of memory processing
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHEN THE NEOCORTEX IS INVOLVED. The span states the view being contradicted in full: 'long-term memory encoding requires early and rapid plasticity within the hippocampus, WHEREAS REORGANIZATION OF THE NEOCORTEX IS LIMITED TO THE LATE STAGES OF MEMORY PROCESSING'. The disagreement is about TIMING - early against late - and not about whether the neocortex reorganises. Q-442.
span.quote: Collectively, these observations have given rise to the prevailing view that long-term memory encoding requires early and rapid plasticity within the hippocampus, whereas reorganization of the neocortex is limited to the late stages of memory processing to subserve remote memory storage and recall ( 11 , 12 ).

span.label: extends → Marr's theoretical modeling work and the standard model of systems-level memory consolidation
span.quote: According to the theoretical modeling work of Marr ( 43 ) and the standard model of systems-level memory consolidation ( 11 ), the hippocampus is believed to integrate input conveyed from distributed neocortical circuits with self-generated spatial information at the time of memory encoding to generate a unified, spatially contextualized memory trace.

span.label: builds-on → recent reports that prefrontal neurons are 'tagged' during encoding and are required for incorporating new information into existing schemas
span.quote: Importantly, our findings are consistent with recent reports suggesting that neurons in the prefrontal cortex are “tagged” during long-term memory encoding ( 16 ) and required for the incorporation of newly learned information into existing neural schemas ( 17 ) and thus suggest that early remodeling of the neocortical architecture may represent a fundamental feature of episodic memory encoding in the brain.
